provenance.title: TB preventive therapy — who is eligible, and the exclusion that must come first
provenance.primarySource: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 1: prevention — tuberculosis preventive treatment (2020), and the collaborative TB/HIV activities policy (2012)
provenance.why: TPT stops latent TB becoming disease in the people most likely to progress — people living with HIV, and young household contacts of a TB case. The one rule that cannot be skipped is the order: active TB must be excluded first, because giving a preventive monotherapy to someone with active disease breeds resistance. So eligibility is a gate behind a gate — exclude active TB, then offer TPT to the right groups.

sourceVerification.note: The WHO TB DAK is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against Module 1 (2020) and the TB/HIV policy; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until the primary text is vendored. The regimen codes (3HP/6H/1HP) are the governed zibo TB value set (V035); the age/weight thresholds here are placeholders pending the national TPT guideline.

rules.name: Active TB not excluded — do not start TPT
rules.message: Do not start TB preventive therapy — active TB has not been excluded.
rules.explanation: TPT is a preventive monotherapy (or a two-drug regimen). Given to someone with undiagnosed active TB it treats disease with too few drugs and breeds resistance. Active TB must be excluded — by symptom screen and, where indicated, a diagnostic test — before TPT.
rules.requiredAction: Investigate and exclude active TB first (symptom screen, and a rapid molecular test if the screen is positive). Only start TPT once active disease is excluded.
sourceRefs: WHO consolidated TB guidelines Module 1 — exclude active TB before TPT

adaptation.whoStatement: Active TB must be excluded before TB preventive treatment is started.

testCases.name: candidate with active TB not excluded is blocked
candidate with active TB excluded is not blocked
not a candidate — rule does not apply

rules.name: Person living with HIV, active TB excluded — offer TPT
rules.message: Eligible for TB preventive therapy — person living with HIV, active TB excluded.
rules.explanation: All people living with HIV in whom active TB has been excluded should be offered TPT, regardless of ART status or degree of immunosuppression. This is the largest single TPT-eligible group and the core of the TB/HIV collaborative package.
rules.requiredAction: Offer TPT (a rifamycin-based regimen such as 3HP where age-appropriate, or 6H) and enrol in a TB_PREVENTION programme to record the course.
sourceRefs: WHO TB/HIV collaborative activities policy; WHO consolidated TB guidelines Module 1

adaptation.whoStatement: All people living with HIV without active TB should receive TPT.

testCases.name: PLHIV with active TB excluded is eligible
PLHIV with active TB not yet excluded is not eligible yet
HIV-negative does not take this rule

rules.name: Young household contact of a TB case, active TB excluded — offer TPT
rules.message: Eligible for TB preventive therapy — child under 5 in household contact with a TB case.
rules.explanation: Children under 5 who are household contacts of a person with TB are at high risk of progression and should receive TPT once active TB is excluded, regardless of tuberculin/IGRA testing where testing is not feasible.
rules.requiredAction: Offer TPT and enrol in a TB_PREVENTION programme. Choose a child-appropriate regimen.
sourceRefs: WHO consolidated TB guidelines Module 1 — household contacts under 5

adaptation.whoStatement: Children under 5 in household contact with a TB case should receive TPT once active TB is excluded.

under-5 contact not yet cleared of active TB is not eligible
older child contact does not take this rule
